findings.evidence: Spectrum.lean:174-179 quantifies over a fresh `A`; the author's own comment at :173 says it is 'stated over a general Dedekind domain because it is applied at two different rings'. Its proof cites only AdicValuation lemmas: `Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/AdicValuation.lean:253 intValuation_le_pow_iff_mem`, `:173 intValuation_apply`, `:94 intValuationDef_if_neg`. Ideal.lean:10-16 is the existing generic complements file, and SInteger/Basic.lean:8 already does `public import TauCeti.RingTheory.DedekindDomain.Ideal`.
findings.fix: Move `le_count_iff_mem_pow` (with its explanatory comment) to `TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Ideal.lean` under `namespace IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum`, drop `private`, and add `public import Mathlib.RingTheory.DedekindDomain.AdicValuation` there. Spectrum.lean already reaches it transitively via SInteger/Basic.lean → TauCeti.RingTheory.DedekindDomain.Ideal, so no new import is needed at the use site.
findings.issue: `le_count_iff_mem_pow` is a general height-one-prime fact over an arbitrary Dedekind domain (`{A : Type*} [CommRing A] [IsDedekindDomain A]`) with no dependence on S-integers, yet it lives privately in the roadmap-specific S-integer spectrum file. TauCeti already has the canonical home for this: `TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Ideal.lean`, docstring 'Complements on the height one spectrum of a Dedekind domain', which exists precisely to hold Mathlib-gap complements about height one primes.

summary: The SInteger directory split was performed correctly and imports are clean, but the general Dedekind-domain lemma `le_count_iff_mem_pow` is buried as a private helper in the downstream S-integer spectrum file instead of the repo's existing complements file.
